chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
If my feet had become firm from these slippery places, I would have altered several things.

key_terms.أَشْيَاءَ: several things (referring to reforms or changes)
key_terms.الْمَدَاحِضِ: the slippery places (metaphor for instability or precarious conditions)
key_terms.قَدَمَايَ: my feet (metaphor for standing firm or stability)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali mean by 'slippery places' in his statement about changing things?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights Imam Ali’s strategic patience (ḥilm) during the early years of his caliphate, where he prioritized consolidating power against internal rebellions like the Battle of the Camel before implementing comprehensive administrative reforms. The metaphor of 'slippery ground' (madāḥiḍ) reflects the political instability and tribal rivalries that necessitated a gradual approach to justice, a theme central to Shia political theology regarding the balance between ideal governance and pragmatic statecraft.
